title: indigo_agent_scheduler: start the first run right after the startup hook when the night start hook names the same task
description:
Observed on the owner's server 2026-11-27 (driver 3.0.0.43, VISIBILITY, site 42N 70E, hooks STARTUP = NIGHT_START = 'Startup', SHUTDOWN = NIGHT_END = 'Shutdown', nautical night): START at 22:30 UTC during the night; the Startup hook ran 22:30-22:33; the first task (Jellyfish Nebula, a setting target, HA +1.3 h) started only at 22:35 with REASON 'Jellyfish Nebula starts at 22:35 UTC, planned for better visibility'. Waiting lost altitude (64.4 deg at 22:33, 64.1 at 22:35); the history shows a single Startup run.

Cause (source analysis, indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/indigo_agent_scheduler.c, to confirm with a test):
1. finish_hook() sets plan_dirty; check_run_end() sets plan_changed because the hook ended 10 s or more off its planned end (estimated duration).
2. process_night() replans first (~2313). The night state is not yet handled/started, and add_plan_hook() (~2860) no longer skips the night start hook of the running hook's task because the hook has finished, so update_plan() adds a NIGHT_START run of 'Startup' (its estimated duration, about 2 min) from now and places the first task after it. update_plan() clears plan_changed (~3158).
3. indigo_scheduler_night_decide() returns SCHEDULER_NIGHT_START and marks the night started; start_night_hook() (~2295) skips it because slot == chain_slot (the task just ran as the previous hook) - correct, the task runs once.
4. select_planned() replans (plan_dirty); the new plan has no night start hook, but plan_changed is already false, so the previous plan is passed with its starts and kept, and the first run keeps the start behind the phantom hook.

Expected: the first run starts when it would without the skipped hook (at once here). Fix options: have add_plan_hook() leave out a night start/resume hook whose task equals chain_slot with chain_ok (mirroring start_night_hook()), and/or decide the night boundary before the first replan, and/or not let a replan that included a hook later skipped clear plan_changed. Also: the REASON text 'planned for better visibility' (~3187) is printed for every future planned start; word it neutrally, or only claim better visibility when the wait gains quality.

Tests: integration test in indigo_test/integration/test_agent_scheduler.c with STARTUP and NIGHT_START naming the same task, START during the night, the hook ending off its estimate, a setting target: the task starts right after the hook and no plan entry/REASON refers to a night start hook; also the case of different tasks for STARTUP and NIGHT_START still runs both. Bump the driver version; update SCHEDULER.md if behaviour text changes.

outcome.summary: Independent review: pass. Root cause confirmed: after a shared STARTUP/NIGHT_START hook ends, finish_hook sets chain_slot (1684), process_night replans before indigo_scheduler_night_decide; add_plan_hook planned NIGHT_START at from=now, update_plan cleared plan_changed, start_night_hook then skipped the task (2295), and select_planned kept the stale start. The new condition (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:2876, slot == chain_slot && time <= now) matches start_night_hook, whose skip depends only on slot == chain_slot (chain_ok only changes standby), for both NIGHT_START and NIGHT_END; RESUME is never planned. chain_slot persists until the next decision that starts a task (1876) or runs nothing (2620, 2518), so the plan and the runtime skip stay consistent: a future night start (time > now, START by day) is still planned; a failed previous hook (chain_ok false) is skipped at runtime too; an UNSAFE-interrupted hook clears chain_slot, so the hook stays planned and runs. Tests: test 1 fails on an unfixed build (Prepare completed 1795734289, Setting started 1795734349, assertion at test_agent_scheduler.c:2173) and passes with the fix (same second); test 2 passes both ways and guards against dropping a different NIGHT_START task. Margin is 5 s against a 60 s defect. Minor, not blocking: the count_plan_items(hook night start)==0 assertion (test_agent_scheduler.c:2175) runs after the target started, when the night has started and no night start item can appear anyway, so it adds little; the timing assertion carries the test. Docs (SCHEDULER.md, SCHEDULER_COMPARISON.md, INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md) are accurate, git grep finds no leftover old REASON text, no README changes, DRIVER_VERSION 0x0300002B->0x0300002C. Ran: the two cases with the fix (pass, pass), the two cases on a scratch build without the fix (fail, pass), full make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler: 200 run, 200 passed, 0 failed.

Reproduction: new integration case visibility_shared_startup_and_night_start_hook_does_not_delay_the_first_run (VISIBILITY, START in the night, STARTUP=NIGHT_START=Prepare with @duration 1 ending after ~1 s, setting target at HA +1.3 h) failed on the unfixed driver: Prepare completed 1795733570, Setting started 1795733630 (60 s behind the planned phantom night start hook). After the fix in add_plan_hook() (a hook due now whose task is chain_slot is not planned, mirroring start_night_hook()) it starts in the same second. visibility_startup_and_night_start_hooks_run_in_order passes before and after. Full make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler: 200 run, 200 passed, 0 failed. flow check (whitespace) passed.
